newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures end dull trading weaker.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures end dull trading weaker.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures ended a dull pit trading session weaker.

Key units barely downticked again in the final 30 minutes as U.S. Treasury bond futures pared losses and U.S. stocks stretched higher, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average advancing more than 50 points.
Except yen, most futures had drifted in tight afternoon ranges and closer to session lows in very quiet trading.
"Anytime it ticked one way or the other, they rang a bell and gave out free sandwiches," joked one IMM floor broker of afternoon trade. "It was really dead."
Yen drifted in the plus column, still underpinned by recent jawboning from U.S. and Japanese government officials that fanned fears of central bank intervention.

Japanese Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara said early Wednesday recent yen moves were clearly excessive and that he shared U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin's view that authorities should intervene "when we think we can win."
One floor broker noted recurrent rumors Wednesday that the Bank of Japan had intervened, and he added that if the rumors were true the market easily shrugged off the action.
Yen glossed over remarks by economist Fred Bergsten.
Bergsten, a prominent private economist, said the United States and Japan should intervene to push up yen.
Traders instead were more focused on how the U.S. trade gap, especially with Japan, shaped up in February after comments early Wednesday by U.S. trade representative Charlene Barshefsky.
She said the United States was concerned about its trade imbalance with Japan and that Washington did not wish to see the gap grow wider.
The overall U.S. trade deficit was expected to shrink to $10.1 billion from January's original $12.71-billion gap.

Also due Thursday, weekly U.S. jobless claims were seen dipping 1,000 to 317,000 from the prior week's original 318,000 levels. April's Philadelphia Federal Reserve survey was seen at 20.4 versus 21.1, and the preliminary April University of Michigan index was forecast at 99.8 from 100.0.
After strong March U.S. capacity use/industrial output data, June yen backed off from $0.008039, 125.50 spot.

June yen settled up $0.000020 to $0.008023, marks lost $0.0009 to $0.5810, Swiss lost $0.0032 to $0.6840, pound fell $0.0042 to $1.6230, Canada rose $0.0005 to $0.7191, Aussie fell $0.0023 to $0.7716, Mex peso rose $0.000150 to $0.122925.
